validated_findings.original_finding: Function accesses file by pk directly without proper ownership validation
validated_findings.evidence: The download function (line 308) has @login_required but the authorization logic at line 314 only checks project membership via file.project.users_assigned.filter(id=request.user.id).exists() rather than checking that the user owns the specific file. This allows any member of a project to download any file in that project.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker who is a member of a project can change the file_id parameter in the URL to download any file in that project, even if they don't own that file.
validated_findings.remediation: Add specific file ownership verification in addition to project membership check

validated_findings.original_finding: Function fetches File by pk (file_id) directly from URL parameter without proper ownership validation
validated_findings.evidence: The download function (line 308) fetches File by pk directly from URL parameter. The logic at line 314: 'if file.project.users_assigned.filter(id=request.user.id).exists():' allows access to any file in the project, not just files owned by the user.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker can enumerate project files by changing file_id in URL and download any file in the project they belong to, violating object-level authorization.
validated_findings.remediation: Ensure file ownership is verified before allowing download, not just project membership

validated_findings.original_finding: Function fetches user profile by user_id directly from URL parameter without checking if requesting user has permission to view that profile
validated_findings.evidence: The download_profile_pic function (line 327) fetches user profile by user_id directly from URL parameter WITHOUT any authorization checks. Any authenticated user can access any user's profile picture by changing the user_id parameter.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker can change the user_id parameter in the URL to download any user's profile picture, violating object-level authorization.
validated_findings.remediation: Add authorization check to ensure user can only view their own profile or profiles they're authorized to view

validated_findings.original_finding: Function uses @login_required but then manually checks for 'auth.change_group' permission which could be bypassed if not properly enforced
validated_findings.evidence: The manage_groups function (line 193) uses @login_required but then manually checks 'auth.change_group' permission at line 164. However, it should be restricted to superusers or staff only. The function lacks specific privilege enforcement.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker who can log in and has 'auth.change_group' permission can access this function, but this permission should be more restricted.
validated_findings.remediation: Restrict manage_groups to superusers only using @user_passes_test(lambda u: u.is_superuser)

validated_findings.original_finding: Function accepts userid and taskid parameters via POST that could be tampered with to assign tasks to unauthorized users
validated_findings.evidence: The manage_tasks function (line 120) accepts userid and taskid parameters via POST and assigns tasks without verifying that the user has permission to assign tasks or that the task belongs to a project they can access.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker who can access the manage_tasks endpoint can manipulate the userid and taskid parameters to assign tasks to unauthorized users or to tasks they shouldn't be able to access.
validated_findings.remediation: Add verification that user has proper permissions to assign tasks and that tasks belong to projects they can access

validated_findings.original_finding: URL patterns /manage_groups/$ and /manage_projects/$ are directly accessible by URL without sufficient authorization checks in views
validated_findings.evidence: Both /manage_groups/ and /manage_projects/ URL patterns are accessible directly. The views themselves do have @login_required but the authorization logic is insufficient and should be more restrictive.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker who knows these URLs can access them directly, though authentication prevents completely unauthorized access.
validated_findings.remediation: Add more restrictive authorization checks to these administrative functions

validated_findings.original_finding: TaskViewSet filters querysets by user but only for non-staff users - staff can see all tasks, potentially allowing privilege escalation
validated_findings.evidence: The TaskViewSet get_queryset method (lines 60-64) allows staff users to see all tasks instead of only those they're assigned to, creating a privilege escalation vulnerability.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: A staff user can access all tasks in the system, potentially viewing confidential information they shouldn't have access to.
validated_findings.remediation: Restrict staff users to see only tasks they're assigned to, not all tasks

validated_findings.original_finding: UserProfileViewSet filters querysets by user but staff can see all profiles - this may allow unauthorized access to user information
validated_findings.evidence: The UserProfileViewSet get_queryset method (lines 182-186) allows staff users to see all profiles instead of restricting to their own or specific profiles.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: A staff user can access all user profiles, potentially viewing sensitive personal information they shouldn't have access to.
validated_findings.remediation: Restrict staff users to see only their own profile or profiles they're authorized to view

validated_findings.original_finding: ProjectViewSet filters querysets by user but staff can see all projects - this may allow unauthorized access to project information
validated_findings.evidence: The ProjectViewSet get_queryset method (lines 93-97) allows staff users to see all projects instead of restricting to projects they're assigned to.
validated_findings.exploit_scenario: A staff user can access all project information, potentially viewing confidential project details they shouldn't have access to.
validated_findings.remediation: Restrict staff users to see only projects they're assigned to, not all projects

overall_assessment.summary: The Django application has severe broken access control vulnerabilities, particularly around IDOR (Insecure Direct Object References) and improper authorization in both traditional Django views and DRF ViewSets. Staff users can access all user data and projects, and several endpoints allow unauthorized access to user profiles and files through parameter manipulation. These issues create serious privilege escalation and data exposure risks. The false positive findings were based on incorrect assessments that authentication was missing when it was actually present.
